item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello, everybody. I guess call me Ainulindale (Ay-noo-LIN-duh-lay). I've been reading "The Silmarillion" and since character names are difficult to obtain as a user id, I went with the name of the first story. I just discovered SCP by accident and it was exactly what I needed to find but didn't know I was looking for.

While watching youtube videos about different gods/angels/esoteric writings (Nag Hammadi library, for example) and a video called something like "SCPs that could end the world" was in the suggestion list. When I googled SCP, I saw what it was and immediately became excited. I've been published, but I pretty much stopped a while ago. I feel that working to write for the SCP Foundation will help me hone my writing skills once more. I'm still familiarizing myself with the SCP universe but I will eventually contribute. I want to do it right though and will be looking to you all for guidance. Thanks for making and maintaining such a great project!

item.content:encoded:
Hello nice to meet you all,

This is an apology. Not the old school apology where the word means a defense thing. And I'm already fucking this up.

I came here with a skewed mindset. I thought that the dramatizations and summaries represented a simple story, written by anyone became a story. So, yeah. That's pretty dumb.

Where was I? Ah, yes. Hello. Great to meet you all.

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers
item.content:encoded:
Do you remember, the twenty-first night of September… oh wait wrong month.

Hello everyone! My name is Morgane, I am 25 years old, I live in France.

I first came across the SCP Foundation wiki three or four years ago, I think. I don't remember how I arrived here (I often find things through clicking on links at half-random, following the flow of my mind.) I joined the French branch in 2017 but didn't do anything there, save from opening a (quite empty) Sandbox.

I have regained interest in the SCP Foundation wiki quite recently, and I thought I may enjoy giving a comment or two, or maybe even trying to write one idea I have for a SCP article (if I ever have the energy to do so), so I decided to join the main site.

I currently have no hobbies due to depression problems, but once I feel better, I intend to pursue my former hobbies: doodling, learning to play the piano, composing music, imagining a fictional language and a fictional country… Something I still keep doing, however, is reading webcomics.

Things that keep me up at night? Loneliness, trauma, and the aforementioned depression. To ignore them, I spend a lot of time on the internet, resulting in short nights. Ha!

I am happy to join this corner of the Internet.

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded: Hey there guys, hope you're doing well. Guess I'll introduce myself. When I was younger I loved reading, but for some reason I dropped it along the way. The SCP foundation gave me the chance to rediscover my old passion (and the stuff here certainly is better than those old child books). I've been a long time reader (maybe 2 years?), and due to not-so-good circumstances in my life I thought it would be nice to test myself as a writer, develop new skills and overall improve as a person trough something I really enjoy. Aside from that, there's not much else to say. My life mostly consist of studying, listening to weird music and playing my guitar. Also, English is not my native language so please excuse me if what I write seems messy. I hope we can all coexist and contribute to the wiki in a positive way!

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello Dr Ivan Hext and welcome to the Wiki! I'm a site author and member of the Community Outreach Team, and this comment is a little info list of resources that will hopefully help you with your journey through the site. We're very happy to see new people excited about writing for the Wiki like you. :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting.

For hashing out concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey!

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing! Take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Readers & Reviewers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Readers & Reviewers
item.content:encoded:
Howdy! I stumbled upon the Foundation a few years ago via a simple google search. (Who would've thought?) Since then, the Foundation has endlessly inspired me and I regularly discuss it with the handful of fellow skippers I know in real life. I'm so grateful that I actually took the time to become a member.

Currently, I plan to read, comment, vote and–when I have a little more experience under my belt–review. Me and my friend (who, despite my best efforts, is not yet a member of this site) have an idea for an SCP in the works, but it's still in the very early stages.

For the monthly question: I often lay awake at night, pondering my future career. Also, I must confess that I have a habit of watching SCP Illustrated immediately before bed, and I'm sure you can imagine how that turned out.

Overall, I am extremely happy and proud to call myself a member of this amazing site! See you around!

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hi everybody!

My name's Patrick, I suppose it'd be appropriate to link to my Twitter and Medium pages once I've qualified for an author's page, somehow I imagine that is gauche at this stage.

I'm 35, founder of a cryptocurrency derivatives layer protocol, active Bitcoin trader, former social games designer and indie game designer. Co-founded a blog about indie games called Play This Thing! with an older GD in '07. Wrote my first short story when I was 7 about a dragon that gets progressively bigger as it eats things until it achieves the scale of celestial bodies (which in retrospect is very SCP-ish). Wrote a novel when I was 17 which was basically a less-good highschool themed take on Rules of Attraction. Went to college for creative writing after dropping out of CS to focus on designing/producing videogames. Started and failed to complete a number of novels. Started writing sci-fi actively in 2012/13, then lapsed a few years focusing on my career in Bitcoin protocol extension, then stated actively again in 2019.

+ show block
– hide block

I've never been a big horror fan, except for zombies and other things with some balance and procedurality. Getting creeped out by some of the classic SCP articles (Reagan-cut-up ending still hits), probably the first time I was experiencing the genre the way most horror fans do. I'm attracted to the sci-fi and abstraction elements of the verse, the extreme ontological flexibility, and the campy surrealism of the media SCPs, which seems to be my niche.

I went in guns blazing yesterday with my first two scips and got nary an upvote, because, execution/details and tangents aside, I think riding the line between mundane, crappy modern world phenomena and anomalies has to be done with great precision to stay on-theme in the verse. It's ok, they were expendable. I'd rather get a comment from a physics PhD, describing the nuances of candling distant galaxies than an upvote, if I have to choose. Of 12 I've drafted in a manic (perhaps anomalous?) frenzy over the past week I think the best ones related to media and narratology/pataphysics so I'm engaging with the community to iterate on those. I have several ideas for canon/mythos extension and film adaptations, and I am *very* open to collaboration. I enjoy giving feedback on concepts and may volunteer for a flight onto the review crew in Q1 '21, if IRL commitments give me the time. I'd like to see some arc of development in the meta-mythos (plausibly deniable metaplot that spans multiple canons) and am super open to collaboration and constellation/collation about that.

I really like the idea of the wiki becoming this uber-House-of-Leaves hypertext construct that acts as a sort of mythology of hypermodernity. I like the idea of 6 series being hypermodernity themed and the eventual 7 series being transhumanism themed. I prefer a Chaos Insurgency that involves subversion and infiltration to the transhuman-reinforced-skeleton soldiers, rather, I think the dystopic trend in the Foundation going in that direction is very interesting.

I have experience running treasury/admin on an actual semi-esoteric foundation relating to building a cryptocurrency protocol (funded by the first ICO in 2013). In 2015 I called out the former director for basically embezzling 200k+, a year later I sort of got end-run by a fellow board member, the co-founder of Tether, and branched out on my own. So I have a lot of insights into Foundation governance and coups that I think, could combine with some other author's styles, and reinforce the meta-mythos and the Inside Baseball of Foundation life for Class 3-5 personnel.

My favorite SCP-001 proposal is Lily's "Beautiful Day". I think the verse could use more of that uncannily heavenly vibe.

Ok that's enough wall of text. I'm seasoned enough in writing not to make it all about my ego as an artist, iteration is the key, anyone please feel free to DM me links to concepts/drafts/headcanon ideas.

Cheers!


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

Hello, everyone!
I'm OhTheHumanity, and I've loved SCP for a long time. I'm an avid creative writer and I thoroughly enjoy the Foundation style. I've made myriad fan-SCPs, of varying style and content. With me, there's no planning on making any specific "kind" of SCPs- not scary, not weird, or anything like that. I just run with an idea and see where it goes! That's the best way to write, I'm told.

Glad to see you're so enthusiastic about writing for the site. When starting off, I highly recommend checking out some of the newer articles on the site to gauge what people are interested in these days. I personally suggest reading SCP-5040. Anyway, here are some resources that will help you out:

◎ Open Resources ◎
◉ Close Resources ◉

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts.

Sandbox

For hashing out concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by the community if you need help refining your concept.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out our Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular, recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community.

With that said, I hope your time on the site is great.

item.content:encoded:
Hello everyone, I am so excited to at long last join the SCP community! I've been aware of SCP for quite a long time and last year was my deep dive into the wiki itself. I've always wanted to discuss my favorite skips and rate them. I hope in the future I'll get around writing something, but for now I'll stick to reading; it's always been one of my favorite hobbies!

For the monthly question: I often wonder how my future will turn out. In most nights however, I wonder how humanity's future will turn out.
